intent: Kept: five sensors at x -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps, y 0.03, 16 mm footprints, body_width 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, mass 0.8, body_length 0.18. Changed: wheel_track from 0.10 back to 0.12, the iteration-5 platform. Expected result: scores return to about 110 to 120, slalom line loss about 0.1, and oval progress back near 0.5. Considering, not committed: a midpoint inertia (mass 0.75, body_length 0.16) only if slalom line loss stays at or below 0.1 with the controller unchanged. learning: Iterations 6 to 8 show that wheel_track 0.10 cost line retention and progress with no gain in max_error, so 0.12 is the better track width on this platform. If this race reproduces about 111.8, the platform is confirmed as the baseline and the remaining lever is inertia at the midpoint. If max_error still reads about 0.062 m with the same progress, that confirms max_error tracks the run-ending threshold, so progress and line loss should be the scoring signals I track.
rationale:
Iterations 6, 7 and 8 all used wheel_track 0.10 and all scored worse than the iteration-5 platform (111.80). Narrowing the track raised slalom line loss from 0.10 to 0.35 and halved oval progress from 0.55 to 0.28. The kp change to 2.5 (iteration 7 at 79.60, and iteration 8 at 77.55 with the same geometry) did not recover it, so the narrow track is the problem, not the gain. The Integrator's entityR1 feedback asks for wheel_track 0.12 to be restored if slalom line loss stays at 0.2 or higher, and it does (0.35 at kp 3.0, 0.00 to 0.1 across the kp 2.5 runs, but oval progress stayed at 0.30). I am taking that advice. I am reverting wheel_track to 0.12 and restoring the iteration-5 platform exactly: mass 0.8, body_length 0.18, sensors at y 0.03 with x from -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps, 16 mm footprints, wheel_radius 0.03.

The max_error values sit at 0.061 to 0.066 m on every geometry tried. That is consistent with the run-ending threshold (off-track limit 0.06 m), not with a tracking limit. Runs end once the error crosses the limit, so max_error mostly records where each run stopped. The more useful measures are progress before exit and line loss. Lower inertia (iteration 4) gave the best progress (124.20) but slalom line loss of 0.85. Restoring mass 0.8 and body_length 0.18 keeps slalom line loss at 0.10 but gives up that progress gain. I expect a score near 111.8 (range 110 to 120), with slalom line loss near 0.1. I am not changing the sensor span, forward offset or footprint, because line loss is controllable at this span and those are settled.
